title: Workday Tutorials
content_markdown:
## About Workday

Log into Workday to complete essential tasks like registering for courses, updating your personal information, paying your tuition, and downloading important documents\.

[Log into Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)

[UBC student uses Workday on her laptop in a study space with other students in the background](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/04/home_workday_intro.jpg)

### [Navigating Workday](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/navigating-workday/)

Find out how to access your personal, financial, and academic records and documents in Workday and the UBC Official Documents tool \(ODMT\)\.

### [Personal information](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/personal-information/ "Go to tutorials")

Get details on how to update your personal information in your account, including citizenship status, third\-party authorization, and emergency contacts\.

### [Course registration](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/ "Go to tutorials")

Learn how to search courses, create a saved schedule, add or drop course sections, and find your registration appointment\.

### [Degree planning](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/degree-planning/ "Go to tutorials")

Follow instructions to declare or change your program of study in Workday and review your transfer credits and grades\.

### [Finances](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/finances/)

Learn how to pay your tuition and student fees\.

### [Student documents](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/student-documents/)

Download your Confirmation of Enrolment Letter and more\.

### [UBC advisor contacts](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/ubc-advisor-contacts/ "Go to tutorials")

Find your Enrolment Services or Accessibility Advisor in Workday\.

title: Logging into Workday
content_markdown:
## About Workday

UBC students use the Workday student information system to access student records, including the following:

-   Course schedule and registration
-   Grades
-   Awards
-   Tuition summary and payment
-   Exam schedule
-   Transcripts
-   Transfer credits
-   Your personal and contact information

## UBC applicants

If you’re an undergraduate applicant who has just applied to UBC, please log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) to access your application status and information\.

## Former students and alumni

Your access to Workday will expire approximately 18 months after you become an inactive student \(e\.g\. after graduation or last registration activity\)\. To order a transcript or replacement document, or download a tax form, log in to the [UBC Online Document tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) \(ODMT\) with your CWL\.

## How to login to Workday

Log in to Workday at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/) with your Campus\-wide Login \(CWL\)\. 

If you don’t have a Student CWL, you can create one after accepting your offer and receiving a student number\. You can [set up a Student CWL](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/how-create-account) through UBC IT\. If you do not have Multi\-factor Authentication set up, [follow instructions](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/multi-factor-authentication-mfa#getting-started) online, then log into Workday\.

## How to change or reset your CWL password

You can change your CWL password after logging in to your [Campus\-Wide Login \(CWL\) myAccount](https://www.myaccount.ubc.ca/myAccount/login.xhtml)\. You can also [reset your CWL password](https://www.myaccount.ubc.ca/myAccount/forgot/forgotPassword.xhtml) if needed through the website\.

For more information, read the [UBC IT article](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/problems-your-cwl) for instructions and troubleshooting support\.

## If you forgot your student number or CWL username

Your UBCcard has your student number printed on it, which is an 8\-digit number\. If you’ve lost your UBCcard, you can [request a new card](https://ubccard.ubc.ca/card-renewals-lost-stolen-cards/loststolen-cards?login)\.

If you forgot your CWL username, you can start the [account recovery process](https://www.myaccount.ubc.ca/myAccount/forgot/forgotLogin.xhtml) or contact [UBC IT](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/problems-your-cwl)\.

title: Updating your contact information
content_markdown:
To receive emergency updates and other important information from UBC, please check that your contact information is up\-to\-date and accurate on Workday\.

## How your information will be used

**Your privacy matters\. Here are some important things to know about your information in Workday:**

-   All contact information is kept private and will not be visible to anyone other than staff and faculty\. 
-   Your contact email will be used by UBC administrative offices for UBC business purposes or to send you university\-related communications\.
-   If you’re a student working for UBC, your contact information will be updated automatically on both your student and employee profile\.

## How to add or edit your contact information

### Go to your personal information in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Personal” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Personal Information”\. 
4.  In the “Change” menu, select the “Home Contact Information” button\. 

### Add or update your contact information

1.  Use the following buttons to make changes:
    -   The pencil icon allows you to edit your information\.
    -   The “X” icon allows you to delete your information\.
    -   The “Add” button allows you to add new information\.
2.  Click the “Submit” button\.

Note: Please monitor your primary email address, as not all UBC communications are sent to secondary email addresses\.

### Update your contact information

1.  Click the “Edit” button to update your contact information\.
2.  Read the information in blue text\.
3.  Use the following buttons to make your changes:
    -   **Pencil icon**: edit your information\. 
    -   **“Add” button**: add new information\.
    -   **“X” icon**: delete your information\. If you haven’t added any contact information yet, you’ll receive an error\.
4.  Click the orange “Submit” button to save your edits\.

> Reminder: Please ensure you have also entered [emergency contact details](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-emergency-contacts/), so that UBC knows who to contact in the event of an emergency affecting you\.

title: Updating your pronouns, trans experience, and gender identity
content_markdown:
## Important information about pronouns and gender identity in Workday

-   Adding this information in Workday is optional and you can change or remove your information at any time\. 
-   If you are a student who also works at UBC, you may need to add your gender identity for health benefits\. 
-   The pronouns you select in Workday will be listed on your profile under your name\. Professors, advisors, and Student Services staff will be able to view this information\.
-   Your trans experience will not be visible to professors, advisors, or Student Services staff\.
-   Your gender identity will only be visible to Student Services staff who require it for UBC purposes\.

## How to add or update your pronouns, trans experience, and gender identity

### First, go to your Profile in Workday

title: Adding your emergency contacts
content_markdown:
## Important information about emergency contacts

-   All UBC students must add emergency contact information in Workday\. 
-   If you are a student who works for UBC,  you will need to add emergency contacts in both your student and employee Workday profiles\.
-   The “Third party user” record on the “Friends and Family” tab is not used for third\-party authorization for UBC business processes\. Find out how to [add a third\-party authorization](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-third-party-authorization/)\.

title: Adding your third-party authorization
content_markdown:
If you want to give someone permission to access your academic or financial record, or to pick\-up documents on your behalf, you can grant them third\-party authorization\. 

Learn more about [third\-party authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/)\. 

> – You may enter up to three authorized third parties\.  
> – Authorized third parties can contact UBC for your information but cannot act on your behalf \(e\.g\. order transcripts, request refunds\)\.  
> – You must complete every field in the third\-party authorization form\. You can choose which permissions to grant to your third party

## How to add or change third\-party authorizations

### Go to your personal information in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Click your user icon in the top right corner, then click the “View Profile” button\.   
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/02/Profile_box.png)
3.  In your profile, click the “Personal” menu item under “Summary”\. **Do** **not** select “Personal” in the left sidebar\.  
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/02/Personal_box.png)
4.   Click the “Additional Data” tab in the top menu\.   
    

### Add or update your third\-party authorizations

1.  Scroll down to find the “Third Party Authorization” section\. 
2.  Click the “Edit” button\. 
3.  Read the instructions and terms of use for third\-party authorizations\. 
4.  Fill out all fields in this section\. You do not have to grant your third\-party all permissions, but you do need to input a response in each field\. 
    -   The “Authorization code” is a code you create and share with your third\-party contact so UBC can verify their identity\. This can be a word, a number, or any combination of letters, numbers or symbols\. 
5.  Click the “OK” button to save your third\-party authorization information\.

title: Updating your preferred name
content_markdown:
## Important information about preferred names

-   Your preferred first and last names will be used for your [UBC Card](https://ubccard.ubc.ca/), Canvas account, and class lists\.
-   If you do not add a preferred name, your preferred name will be your legal name\.
-   If you have not enrolled in UBC since 2021, you may not have access to Workday\. In this case, you will not be able to update your name on your student record through Workday\. Please contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors) for assistance instead\.

## How to update your preferred names 

### First, go to your Profile in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  On the Workday home screen, click your user icon in the top right corner\.
3.  Click the “View Profile” button in the pop up menu\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/04/home_view-profile.png)

### Next, go to your personal information

1.  Click the “Personal” tab in the left menu\. 
2.  Click the “Names” tab in the top menu\. Your legal name and preferred name will be shown in this view\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Updating-your-preferred-name_go-to-personal-information.jpeg)

title: Adding your Social Insurance Number (SIN) or Individual Tax Number (ITN)
content_markdown:
> If you have a previous student or employee record at UBC, you may see an alert indicating that the national identifier \(SIN\) you entered is already in use\. This is expected\. Please dismiss the alert, ensure all required fields are completed, and then submit your update\.

If you’re a former student or alumni who can’t log into Workday, contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for support with adding or updating your SIN or ITN\. Learn more about a [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) or [Individual Tax Number \(ITN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn/)\.

## **How to add or edit your SIN or ITN**

### **Go to your personal information in Workday**

1\. Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\.  
2\. Click the user icon in the top right corner, then click the “View Profile” button\.

[Select the view profile icon on right side of the screen](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/02/Profile_box-293x300.png)

3\. In your profile, click the “Personal” tab\. Do not select the “Personal” menu category from the left sidebar\.

[Select Personal under Summary, not from side bar navigation](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/02/Personal_box-768x485.png)

4\. Click the “IDs” tab in the top menu\.

### **Add or update your SIN or ITN**

1.  Click the “Edit” button\.
2.  To update your SIN, click the plus sign in the top left of the “National IDs” table **OR** to update your ITN, click the plus sign in the top left of the “Government IDs” table\.
3.  Complete the required fields:
    -   Click the “Country” box and enter “Canada”\.
    -   Click the “ID type” box and enter “Social Insurance Number” or “Individual Tax Number”\. Add your ID number\.
        -   For a SIN, add your number in the “Add/Edit ID” box\.
        -   For an ITN, add your ID number in the “Identification \#” box\.
    -   Update the “Issued Date” and “Expiration Date” boxes\.
4.   Please check that the information is correct before proceeding, since you will not be able to see your SIN or ITN numbers in full through your Workday profile\.
5.  Click the “Submit” button\.

### **View your changes**

You can view your changes and confirm that your SIN or ITN has been added to your record by returning to your IDs view on your “Personal” tab in your profile\.

You will see that you have a SIN or ITN on record\. However, your number will not be shown on screen\. Instead, you will see “XXX XXX XXX”\.

## **If you have questions**

If you have questions about adding your Social Insurance Number or Individual Tax Number contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Viewing the course schedule
content_markdown:
## How to view the course schedule

### Go to your Academics app

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Academics”\. 

### Find course sections

1.  Select the “Registration & Courses” tab in the top menu\.  
2.  Click the “Find Course Sections” link in the “Registration” menu to the right\. 

#### Select the academic term or session

In the pop\-up menu, select the Term or Session you want to find course sections for:  

1.  Click the “Start Date within” field\.  
2.  If you are exploring courses for the upcoming year, select “Future Periods”\. 
    -   Make sure you choose the correct campus \(i\.e\., UBC\-O for the Okanagan campus, UBC\-V for the Vancouver campus\)\. 
3.  For Winter registration, each Term must be selected individually\. 
    -   Select one or both Winter Term 1 and/or Winter Term 2 \.
    -   **Do not** choose the option that combines Winter Term 1 and Winter Term 2 as it will not display the courses\. 

[find course sections](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/02/view-course-schedule-768x510.png)

4\. For Summer registration, select the applicable Academic Session\.

#### Select your academic level

1.  Click the “Academic Level” field\. 
2.  Select ‘Undergraduate’ \(e\.g\. bachelor’s degree programs\) or ‘Graduate’ \(e\.g\. master’s degree and PhD programs\) from the list\.   
    -   **Do not** select “Academic Level Not Applicable”\. This will result in an error\. 
3.  Click the “OK” button\. 

#### **Filter your search results**

title: Resolving a hold on your record
content_markdown:
> **Reminder:**  
> – A hold on your record may block you from registering in courses or receiving a transcript or parchment\.      
> — Please note that a “Missing Direct Deposit Bank Account” hold will not prevent you from registering in courses or receiving a transcript or parchment\.  
> – Check and resolve your holds before your registration appointment to avoid any issues registering in courses\.  

## How to resolve a hold on your record

### Go to your action items and holds in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\.   
2.  Click your user icon in the **top right corner,** then click the “View Profile” button\.
3.  In your profile, click the “Action Items and Holds” tab\. 
4.  View your current holds in the “Active Holds” tab in the top menu

### Resolve your hold

Complete the action items listed in your Active Hold under “Resolution Instructions”\. For example, you may have to pay overdue tuition and fees, or you may need to see an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) or [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) before registering in courses

### Confirm that your hold has been removed

If you’re able to complete the actions, your hold may be resolved automatically\. Depending on the type of hold, processing times can vary\. To verify this, visit the “Action Items and Holds” page and click the “Resolved Holds” tab\.

## If you need additional support

Contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors) if you need help with understanding  a hold on your academic record\. Learn how to find your [Enrolment Services Advisor’s contact information](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/ubc-advisor-contacts/finding-your-enrolment-services-advisors-contact-information/) in Workday\.

title: Adding a program of study (second major or minor)
content_markdown:
## About adding a program of study 

You will only be able to self\-declare in Workday if you meet the program entry requirements\.  

This tutorial covers how to add a second major or a minor program, if you are eligible to do so\. If you haven’t done so yet, find out how to [declare a major or specialization\.](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/degree-planning/declaring-or-changing-your-primary-major-honours-or-specialization/)

## How to add your program of study

### First, go to your Profile in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  On the Workday home screen, click your user icon in the top right corner\.
3.  Click the “View Profile” button in the pop\-up menu\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/04/home_view-profile.png)

### Next, go to your Academics Overview

1.  Click the “Academics” tab in the left menu\.
2.  By default, you’ll be viewing the information under the “Overview” tab in the top menu\.
3.  Click the orange  “Add Program of Study” button at the bottom\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Adding-a-program-of-study_academic-overview-940x314.jpg)

### Add your program of study

1.  In the pop\-up window, search the options to find the program of study you’d like to add\. You can add a second major or a minor program, if your degree allows it\. 
2.  Select the program you want by clicking the circle to the left of the program name in the drop\-down menu\.
3.  Your primary program of study will show up in the “Bundled With” column\. If you have more than one major, all second majors and/or minors must be bundled with the primary program of study\.
4.  In the “Expected Completion Date” column, enter the same completion date as your primary program of study\.
5.  **Do not** change the “Declare Date”, as it will show the current date\.
6.  Click the “Submit” button to save your changes\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Adding-a-program-of-study_add-your-program-940x262.jpg)

### Confirm your changes

After declaring your program, it will show up under your academics overview\. Follow the [previous instructions above](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/adding-a-program-of-study-second-major-or-minor/#academics-overview) to go to your academics overview\. 

## Commonly encountered problems

If you do not see your updated program of study in your academics overview, you may have changed your declare date\.  A request will automatically be sent to a UBC administrator to correct the date before you can update your program again\. 

You will not be able to make any other program changes until this request is resolved\. 

### Faculty approvals

Some Faculties need to approve the change in the system for you to add a program of study\.

If you do not see your program of study change immediately, it may be because your change requires approval and a request has been sent to a UBC administrator\. You will not be able to make any other program changes until your request has been approved or denied\.

You will receive a notification in Workday if your request is denied\. Click on the “Notifications” bell icon in the menu bar to view the details\.

title: Removing your program of study (second major or minor)
content_markdown:
## About removing your program of study

If you are no longer completing your minor or second major, you can follow the instructions below to drop the secondary program from your record\.

You cannot use this process to drop your primary program\.  If you want to stop your studies at UBC or drop the primary program you are currently enrolled in, contact an advisor in your program or faculty to discuss your options\.

## How to remove a program of study

### First, go to your Profile in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  On the Workday home screen, click your user icon in the top right corner\.
3.  Click the “View Profile” button in the pop\-up menu\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/04/home_view-profile.png)

###  Next, go to your academics overview

1.  Click the “Academics” tab in the left menu\.
2.  By default, you’ll be viewing the information under the “Overview” tab in the top menu\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Removing-your-program-of-study_go-to-academic-overview.jpg)

### Remove your program of study

1.  You should see a table with your program of study details\. Click on the white “Request” button next to the program you want to remove\. 
2.  Select “Remove Program of Study” from the drop\-down list\.   
    
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Removing-your-program-of-study_request.jpg)
    
3.  In the “Remove Program of Study” window, find the program to remove and check its box\.  
4.  Check the “Confirm” box\. 
5.  Click the orange “Submit” button at the bottom of the page to save your changes\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Removing-your-program-of-study_remove-your-study.jpg)

### Confirm your changes

Review your academics overview to confirm that your program has been removed\. Follow the [previous instructions above](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/removing-your-program-of-study-second-major-or-minor/#academics-overview) to go to your academics overview\. 

The status for the program of study will change to “Discontinued” when your program is successfully removed\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Removing-your-program-of-study_confirmation-940x276.jpg)

## Faculty approvals

Some faculties need to approve the change in the system for you to remove a program of study\.

If you do not see your program of study change immediately, it is because your change requires approval and a request has been sent to a UBC administrator\. You will not be able to make any other program changes until your request has been approved or denied\.

You will receive a notification in Workday if your request is denied\. Click on the “Notifications” bell icon in the menu bar to view the details\.

title: Viewing your transfer credit or high school and AP/IB Credit
content_markdown:
## About transfer credit

You will only have access to the “Transfer Credit” page in Workday if you have been awarded transfer credit\. Learn more about [transfer credit terms](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/transfer-credit-terms)\.

The following transfer credits are shown in Workday:

-   “Credit from Coursework” refers to transfer credit from other post\-secondary institutions\. 
-   “Credit from Exams” refers to transfer credit from high school and AP or IB coursework\. 

## How to check your transfer credit 

### First, go to your Profile in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  On the Workday home screen, click your user icon in the top right corner\.
3.  Click the “View Profile” button in the pop\-up menu\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/04/home_view-profile.png)

### Next, go to your transfer credit

1.  Once you’re in your profile, click the “Academics” tab in the left menu\. 
2.  In the “Academics” page, click the “Transfer Credit” tab in the top menu\. You will only see this tab in the menu if you have been awarded transfer credit\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Degree-Planning_viewing-your-transfer-credits_go-to-your-transfer-credits.jpg)

### Review your transfer credit

#### Credit from coursework

On the “Transfer Credit” page, under “Credit from Coursework”, you’ll find a table showing the UBC courses and credits you’ve received credit for, along with details of the post\-secondary course and institution where you earned the credits\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Degree-Planning_viewing-your-transfer-credits_credit-from-coursework.jpg)

#### First\-year credit from high school and AP/IB 

On the “Transfer Credit” page, scroll down to “Credit from Exams”\. You’ll find a table showing the UBC courses and credits you’ve received credit for, along with details about the class or high school program where you earned those credits\. 

Find out which Advanced Placement, British\-patterned education, and International Baccalaureate courses are eligible for [first\-year credit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/) at UBC\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Degree-Planning_viewing-your-transfer-credits_first-year-credit-from-high-school.jpg)

## Commonly encountered problems

If you have transfer credits but can’t access the “Transfer Credit” page, or you’re missing transfer credits, contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors)\.

title: Viewing your grades and academic record
content_markdown:
## About your grades and academic record

In Workday, there are 2 different places to find your grades depending on the academic period: 

-   The “View My Grades” page will show you your grades for a specific academic term\. 
-   The “View my Academic Record” page will display your grades for all terms, your cumulative average, your academic standing\. and your Class Standing \(year level\) at the start of the academic period\.

If you don’t see a grade for a course, your professor hasn’t submitted it yet\. 

Visit the UBC Academic Calendar to learn more about [grades](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices/introduction) and [standings](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices/standings)\. 

## How to view your grades and academic record

### Go to your Academics app 

1.   Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Academics”\. 

### View your grades

1.  On the right, in the “Academic Records” menu, click the “View My Grades” link\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Degree-Planning_view-your-grades.jpg)

2.  In the pop\-up window, select the academic year and session you want to see your grades for\.
    -   The “Student Record” field should be filled in automatically with your name and program\. You should not need to change this field unless you have multiple academic records\.
    -   For example, if you are an undergraduate dual degree student, you may need to select the student record for the degree program you want to view\.
3.  Click the orange “OK” button to display your grades\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Degree-Planning_viewing-your-grades_view-your-grades-pop-up-window.jpg)

4.  You’ll be brought to the “View My Grades” page\. Your grades for the selected academic year and session will be listed in a table\.  You can find your Academic Period Average and Cumulative Average under the table\.
    -   Your **Academic Period Average** shows you the average grade you received for the academic period listed\.
    -   Your **Cumulative Average** shows your average grade for all the courses you’ve completed in the academic record you selected in step 2\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Degree-Planning_viewing-your-grades_view-your-averages-1.jpg)

### View your academic record

1.  Follow the [steps above](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/viewing-your-grades-and-academic-record/#go-to-academics-app) to go to the Academics app\. You will be on the “Academics” page by default\.  
2.  On the right, in the “Academic Records” menu, click the “View My Academic Record” link\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Degree-Planning_viewing-your-grades_go-to-view-your-academic-record-940x369.jpg)

3.  You will be taken to the “View My Academic Record” page\. Here, under “Coursework”, you will see a list of your academic sessions\. 
4.  Click the arrow icon on the left of the session you want to view to expand the description\. You will see your courses and grades for the period listed in a table\.  
      
    Below the table, you will also see:
    -   **Your Academic Period** **Totals**, including your grade average for the academic year and the number of credits used to calculate your average\.
    -   **Your Cumulative Average**, which is the average grade of all the courses you’ve completed since you started at UBC\.
    -   **Your Academic Standing**, which reflects your performance in your program\. You may see “Good Academic Standing”, “Academic Probation”, or “Failed Standing”\. Learn more about your [academic standing](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-land-and-food-systems/academic-regulations/year-promotion-and-academic-standing)\. Honours for outstanding academic performance will be listed here as well\. 
    -   Y**our Class Standing at Start of Period**, which reflects your year level at the beginning of the academic period\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/View-your-grades_Academic-Period-Totals-1.jpg)

title: Viewing your academic progress report
content_markdown:
For additional support with navigating or understanding your Academic Progress Report, contact [Academic advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)

## How to find your Academic Progress Report 

### Go to your Academics app in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Academics”\.

### View Academic Progress Report

Click “View My Academic Progress” to view:

-   The academic requirements for each of your programs, including your degree and any specializations  
-   The courses you are registered in or have completed, and how they are being used to meet your requirements  
-   The academic requirements you have not yet completed 
-   Your unused registrations, also known as courses you have registered in that cannot be used to meet your program requirements 
-   Your cumulative average 
-   Academic progress wheel\(s\) for your program\(s\) of study, if in use by your home faculty or school 

#### Academic progress wheel\*

-   The Academic Progress Wheel will show you the percentage of academic requirements you have completed for your program\. There may be one wheel for each program of study\. A program of study can be a major, honours, or minor\. For example, if you are completing both a major and a minor, you may see two progress wheels\.  

-   If you are completing a Co\-op program, you may see a progress wheel tracking your Co\-op requirements\. The wheel will remain at 0% throughout your Co\-op terms but will be updated to show 100% completion after you complete your final work term, indicating that you have fulfilled the Co\-op requirement\. 

\*  Academic Progress Wheel\(s\) may be visible for your program\(s\) of study, if in use by your home faculty or school\. 

### View your overall academic progress

In the “Overall Academic Progress” section, you can see the total number of credits you need to complete your degree \(known as your “Credits Defined”\)\. You can also see your completed credits \(known as your “Credits Satisfying”\), your credits in progress, and the number of credits remaining to complete your program\.  

Please note that Bachelor of Applied Science, Vancouver and Bachelor of Music, Vancouver will not see the “Overall Academic Progress” section\. 

1.  Hover over the magnifying glass in the “Overall Academic Progress” in the first column of the “Overall Academic Progress” table\. Three dots will appear\.  
2.  Click on the three dots to open the “Actions” menu and view the details of your “Total Academic Requirement Assignment”\. This is the number of credits you must complete in total for the program to graduate\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Viewing-your-academic-progress_total-academic-requirement-e1767635677904.jpg)

### Review your credits in progress

To see how the courses you’re currently registered in fulfill the academic requirements of your program:

1.  Click on the down arrow beside the “Credits in Progress” number to open the  drop\-down menu\.  
2.  Click “View Details” on the drop\-down menu\. 
3.  A pop\-up window will appear, listing the courses you’re currently registered in, their academic period, and the academic requirements they meet for your program\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Viewing-your-academic-progress_credits-remaining-e1767635573272.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Viewing-your-academic-progress_credits-pop-up-e1767635060700.jpg)

### Review your completed credits

To see how the courses you’ve completed fulfill the academic requirements of your program: 

1.  Click on the down arrow beside the “Credits Satisfying” number to open the drop\-down menu in the “Overall academic progress” table\. 
2.  Click “View Details” on the drop\-down menu\. 
3.  A pop\-up window will appear, listing the credits you’ve completed already, including their academic period, grade, and the academic requirements they’ve met for your program\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Viewing-your-academic-progress_review-completed-credits-e1767635432227.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Viewing-your-academic-progress_view-completed-credits-pop-up-e1767635321349.jpg)

## Understanding your program requirements

Requirements for certain programs may vary depending on what year you enrolled in your program\. The requirements you see match the version of requirements on the [UBC Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools) that you must follow to complete your program\.  

## About unused registrations 

Unused registrations are courses you have registered in or transfer credit that cannot be used to meet your program requirements\.  

If you have unused registrations, you will see an arrow next to the number\. Click the arrow and a pop\-up window listing the details for your unused registrations will appear\.  

The “Reason” column will explain why a course cannot be used to meet your requirements\. Here are some of the reasons you may see:

-   **In Excess:** This course would meet a requirement you have already fulfilled\.  
-   **Didn’t Match:** This course falls outside of the academic requirements for your program of study\. 
-   **Didn’t Satisfy:** You did not earn credit for this course, or it did not meet any requirement for your program\(s\) of study\.  

## Additional resources

If you want to find out what your progress would be if you transferred to a new program, you can [evaluate your academic requirements](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/degree-planning/evaluate-your-academic-requirements/)\.

title: Declaring or changing your primary major, honours, or specialization
content_markdown:
## About declaring or changing your major

You will only be able to self\-declare your major in Workday if you meet the program entry requirements\.  

You cannot use the steps below to change your degree program\. For example, you cannot change from a Bachelor of Science to a Bachelor of Arts, or from a Bachelor of Arts in Vancouver to a Bachelor of Arts in the Okanagan\. To change your degree program, speak to an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors)\.

### When to use this process: 

-   To declare your primary major, honours, or specialization in your program\.
-   To change your primary major, honours, or specialization to another one\. For example, changing a Bachelor of Arts Major in Psychology to a Bachelor of Arts Major in Sociology\.

## How to declare your primary major

### First, go to your Profile in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  On the Workday home screen, click your user icon in the top right corner\.
3.  Click the “View Profile” button in the pop\-up menu\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/04/home_view-profile.png)

###  Next, go to your academics overview

1.  Click the “Academics” tab in the left menu\.
2.  By default, you’ll be viewing the information under the “Overview” tab in the top menu\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_go-to-academic-overview.jpg)

### Change your program of study

1.  You should see a table with your program of study details\. Click on the white “Request” button in the row of your current primary program of study\.  
    
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_change-program-of-study_request-1-940x242.jpg)
    
2.  In the pop\-up window, remove your current program of study from the “New Program of Study” box by clicking the ‘x’ next to the program name\. This way, you will not need to re\-enter your expected completion date and other details\.  
    
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_change-your-program_remove-current-program.jpg)
    

3.  Search for the program you want to declare as your major or specialization in the “New Program of Study” box\. Make sure you include your degree \(for example, B\.A\.\) in the name of the new primary program of study\. The degree’s initials must also include a period after the letters\. For example, if you are searching for a Bachelor of Arts, type “B\.A\.” not “BA”\.  
    
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_change-your-program_declare-new-major.jpg)
    
4.  Select the program you want from the drop\-down menu\.
5.  If you have bundled programs on your record, such as second majors or minors, you will need to remove your current program of study from the “Bundled With” box by clicking the ‘x’ next to the program name\. Then, enter your new primary program of study in the “Bundled With” field on the same line as your secondary program\.  
    
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_change-your-program_bundled-with-major-1-940x157.jpg)
    
6.  After selecting your primary program of study, click the checkbox in the “Is Primary” column\.
7.  Enter your Expected Completion Date in the right column if it is not automatically populated\. Use the same Expected Completion Date you see on your current primary program of study\. Your Faculty can change this date later if necessary\. You are **not required** to graduate by this date\.
8.  **Do not** change the “Declare Date”, as it will show your current date\.
9.  Click the “Submit” button to save your changes\.   
    
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_change-your-program_submit-new-program-940x230.jpg)
    

### Confirm your changes

Follow the [previous instructions above](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/declaring-or-changing-your-primary-major-honours-or-specialization/#academic-overview) to go to your academics overview\. 

After declaring your new program, it will show up under your academics overview\. The status will show “In Progress”\. 

Your previous primary program of study will also be listed in your academics overview\. The status for this program will show “Discontinued”\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_view-new-major-940x223.jpg)

## Errors and Alerts 

You may come across errors and alert messages when declaring your major: 

-   You may not meet the program entry requirements or you aren’t allowed to self\-declare your selected program\. Contact your faculty or department\.
-   You may not have filled out all required fields\. For example, if you do not enter an “Expected Completion Date”, you will not be able to declare your major\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Declaring-your-major_errors-940x222.jpg)

## Additional resources

-   [Adding a program of study \(second major or minor\)](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/home-page/adding-a-program-of-study-second-major-or-minor/)
-   [Removing a program of study \(second major or minor\)](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/degree-planning/removing-your-program-of-study-second-major-or-minor/)

title: Downloading your Confirmation of Enrolment Letter
content_markdown:
A Confirmation of Enrolment Letter—also known as a Proof of Enrolment or Verification of Enrolment—is an official document showing that you are currently registered at UBC\.

## Access the UBC Official Documents tool \(ODMT\)

UBC students can download Confirmation of Enrolment Letters from the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) \(ODMT\) or through Workday:

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\.
3.  Select “Academics”\.
4.  In the “Transcripts and Enrolment/Completion Letters” menu, click the “UBC Official Documents” link to go to the UBC Official Documents tool \(ODMT\)\.

### How to download your Confirmation of Enrolment Letter 

1.  Select “Confirmation of Enrolment Letter” in the “Order Options” menu\.
2.  Select the academic session\.
3.  Click the “Request Letter \(PDF\)” button\.
4.  Wait a few seconds before clicking the “Generate Letter \(PDF\)” button\.
5.  Click the “PDF” icon to download\.

title: Viewing your registration appointment
content_markdown:
## How to view your registration appointment

### Go to your Academics app

1.   Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Academics”\. 

### Go to your registration appointment

1.  Click the “Registration & Courses” tab in the top menu\.
2.  Your registration appointment date and time will be listed on the right side of the table\. 

> Please note:  
> – Your Workday account may show both a registration appointment **start time and end time**\. While the start time indicates the start of your personal registration period, the end time simply refers to the period when general enrolment begins\. It has no relevance to your registration timeline\.  
> – If you are enrolled in more than one program, you will be assigned two registration appointments\. For example, an undergraduate dual degree student would register in courses for **both** programs on the earliest listed registration appointment date\.  
> – **Your registration date and time may change**, so please check your registration appointment in Workday regularly for updates\. 

## Next steps

To prepare for your course registration, you can [view the course schedule](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/) and [create a saved schedule](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/creating-a-saved-schedule/)\. 

When your registration appointment opens, you can [register from a saved schedule](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/registering-in-courses-from-a-saved-schedule/) or [register for individual course sections](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/registering-for-individual-course-sections/)\.

title: Registering for individual course sections
content_markdown:
> This function will not be available in Workday until your [registration appointment](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-your-registration-appointment/) opens\.

There are two primary ways you can register for courses in Workday:

1.  [Create a saved schedule](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/creating-a-saved-schedule/) and register all your courses at once\.
2.  Register for individual courses one at a time\.

This page explains how you can register for a specific course after your registration opens\. Prior to your registration appointment, you can create a saved schedule and register for multiple courses at once when your registration is open\. 

## How to register for individual course sections 

### Find course sections

Follow the instructions to [view the course schedule](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/)\.

### Select a course section

1.  When you find a course you want to register for, click the course title link\.  
    
    [Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Register-for-individual-course_select-course-section-940x373.jpg)
    
2.  On the “View Course Section” page, review the course description for eligibility requirements, prerequisites, or corequisites to confirm that you are eligible to register\.   
    

### Register in the course section 

1.  Click the “Register” button at the bottom of the page\. 
    -   The button will only appear after your registration appointment when registration has opened for you\. 
    -   If registration is not yet open for you, you can add this course to a saved schedule by clicking the “Add to Saved Schedule” button\. 
2.  On the “Register for Course Section” page, review the selected course section\.
3.  Select the course section you want to register for\. You may see more than one option\. 
4.  Ensure you have selected all activities required for the course \(e\.g\. tutorials, seminars, laboratories, etc\.\)\. 
5.  Click the “Register” button to register in the individual course section\. 
6.  If you do not want to register in the course section, cancel the registration by clicking the “Cancel” button\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Register-for-individual-courses_review-course-section-1.jpg)

### Confirm your registration

A summary page will appear to confirm that you have registered successfully\.  This page will include information about the course section you registered in\.

Click the white “View Registered Courses” button at the bottom of the page to view your full list of registered courses\. You can also click the white “View Student Account” button to view your account summary, where you can review your financial information, like your tuition\.

## Common issues

If you do not see a “Register” button, it may be because registration is not yet open to you\. Check your [registration appointment](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-your-registration-appointment/)\.

If registration for a course section is unsuccessful, find out why:

-   Read the course description for eligibility requirements, prerequisites or corequisites\. 
-   Use the Troubleshoot Registration tool located in the Registration & Courses tab in the Academics app\. Learn more about [troubleshooting course registration](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/troubleshooting-your-course-registration/)\. 
-   Under some circumstances during the registration process, the system will automatically guide you to the Registration Troubleshooting tool\. Follow the prompts to troubleshoot your registration\. 

## Additional resources

-   [Registering from a saved schedule](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/registering-in-courses-from-a-saved-schedule/)
-   [Dropping a course](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/dropping-a-course/)
-   [Swapping a course](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/swapping-a-course/)
-   [Withdrawing from a course](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/withdrawing-from-a-course/)
-   [Troubleshooting your course registration](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/troubleshooting-your-course-registration/)

title: Creating an Evaluated Academic Requirements report
content_markdown:
## About the Evaluated Academic Requirements Report

> To view your academic progress for your **current program\(s\) of study**, follow the tutorial on viewing your [Academic Progress Report](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/viewing-your-academic-progress-report/)\.

The Evaluated Academic Requirements Report is a tool for UBC students who are thinking about declaring a specialization or transferring to a different program of study at UBC\. The report can show you how your academic progress would carry over or be impacted by the change\. It helps to answer the question, “What if I changed my program to this?”

For example, you might wish to change your primary program, also referred to as your major or specialization\. Or, you might want to add or change minors, honours, or second majors, known as secondary programs\.

Here are some things to keep in mind:

-   The Evaluated Academic Requirements report shows what your progress in a new degree program or specialization would be based on your current academic progress and registered courses\.
-   Report results are informational only to help in your degree planning\. 
-   Your report will reflect the most up\-to\-date program requirements\.
-   You can have up to 10 Evaluated Academic Requirements reports in your Workday account at a time\. If you create more than 10, your oldest report will be removed from the system\. 
-   You can only test your academic requirements for a new program of study, not for an individual course registration\. 

## How to create an Evaluated Academic Requirements report 

### Go to your Academics app 

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Academics”\.

### Go to your academic requirements

In the “Academic Planning” menu, click the “Evaluate Academic Requirements” link\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluated-Academic-Requirement_go-to-academic-requirement.jpeg)

Your current programs of study will be displayed in a table format: 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_current-program-940x326.jpg)

### Create a report for a program of study you’re thinking of transferring to

First, scroll down to the “Evaluate Programs of Study” section\. By default, this section will be set to your current program\(s\) of study\.

#### If you are thinking of changing majors or specializations

Your major or specialization is known as your **primary** program of study\.

1.  Remove your “Program of Study” in the first row by clicking the ‘x’ icon\.
2.  Search for and select the new program of study \(major or specialization\) you’re thinking of transferring to\. Be sure to include your degree in your search \(e\.g\. B\.A\. Major in Sociology\)\.
3.  Make sure the “Is Primary” box is selected\.
4.  Keep the “Requirements Effective Date” as is, which is set to the current date by default\.
5.  Click the orange “OK” button\. 
6.  Click the “Done” button to run the evaluation, which will create a report for you in the background\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_evaluate-program-of-study.jpg)

#### If you are thinking of adding a minor, honors, or second major

Minors, honours, or second majors are known as **secondary** programs of study\.

1.  Keep your primary program of study in the first row and make sure the “Is Primary” box is checked\.
2.  Click the \(\+\) icon on the left corner of the table beside “Program of study”\. A new row should be created\.
3.  In this new row, search for and select the secondary program of study you are thinking of adding\.
4.  Make sure the “Is Primary” box is not selected for this row\.
5.  Keep the “Requirements Effective Date” as is, which is set to the current date by default\.
6.  Click the orange “OK” button\. 
7.  Click the “Done” button to run the evaluation, which will create a report for you in the background\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_removing-a-minor.jpg)

#### If you are thinking of changing your minor, honours, or second major

Minors, honours, or second majors are known as **secondary** programs of study\.

1.  Keep your primary program of study in the first row and make sure the “Is Primary” box is checked\.
2.  In the row with your secondary program of study, click the ‘x’ icon to remove the program\.
3.   Search for and select the new secondary program you’re thinking of changing\.
4.   Make sure the “Is Primary” box is not selected for this row\.
5.   Keep the “Requirements Effective Date” as is, which is set to the current date by default\.
6.   Click the orange “OK” button\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_removing-a-minor.jpg)

7.   Click the “Done” button to run the evaluation, which will create a report for you in the background\.

#### If you encounter an error

You may receive a “Page Error” if you do not select a primary program of study\. Please make sure the “Is Primary” box is checked for your main program of study in the “Evaluate Programs of Study” table\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_page-error.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_error-check-primary-940x189.jpg)

You may receive an “Error – Bundled With” alert if you select an additional program of study, like a second major or minor, but do not select a primary program of study to bundle it with\. 

To resolve this issue:

-   Make sure your additional program of study is on its own line below your primary program of study\.
-   Keep the “Is Primary” box unchecked for the additional program\.
-   Find and select your primary program of study in the “Bundled With” field\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_error-bundled-with.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_bundled-with-error-alert-940x407.jpg)

### Find your evaluated academic requirements report

After you’ve run your chosen evaluation, you can access your “Evaluated Academic Requirements” report results in one of three ways:

-   Pop\-up notification
-   Notification menu
-   Academics app

#### Pop\-up notification

A pop\-up notification will appear at the top right of the page once your report has been created\. Click the link in the notification to view your report\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_notification-940x159.jpg)

#### Notification menu

You can also find the new reports in your notifications inbox\.

1.  Click the bell icon in the top right corner of the page to go to your notifications inbox\. 
2.  Click the report notification in the list of notifications\.
3.  Once the notification message is open on the right, click the “View Details” button to review your report\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Evaluate-Academic-Requirements_notification-tab-940x275.jpg)

#### Academics App 

You can access a list of all your previous Evaluated Academic Requirements reports in the Academics App if the notifications are resolved\. This is also the place you can see Evaluated Academic Requirement reports your academic advisor may have run for you\.

1.  Follow the [steps above](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/evaluate-your-academic-requirements/#academics-app) to go to the Academics App\. 
2.  Under the “Academic Planning” menu on the right, click the “View Evaluated Academic Requirements” link\. 
3.  In the pop\-up window, select the Evaluated Academic Requirements report you want to view from the drop\-down menu\.
4.  Click the orange “OK” button to display your report\. 

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/View-Evaluated-Academic-Requirements.jpg)

### Review your academic requirements

The date and evaluated program of study are displayed at the top of the report\. 

Review your results, which look and work like a regular Academic Progress Report, to understand how a change in program would impact your academic progress\.

## Next steps

If you need further help thinking through a program change, contact your [Faculty advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising)\.

title: Troubleshooting course registration
content_markdown:
> If you are experiencing issues when attempting to register from a saved schedule, view the [troubleshooting saved schedules](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/troubleshooting-saved-schedules/) tutorial\.

## Troubleshooting your registration

### Go to your Academics app

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Academics”\. 
4.  In the Registration & Course tab, click on the Troubleshoot Registration link\. 
5.  Review the entire “Troubleshoot Registration” page, including the “Course” and “Course Section” tables, to understand the eligibility issues that will prevent you from registering \(after your registration appointment opens\)\. There may be more than one reason\. 

#### Using the Registration Troubleshooting tool

Enter individual courses or course sections to identify and troubleshoot potential registration issues during or before registration\.  

You don’t need to wait until your registration appointment opens to run registration Troubleshooting\. However, the results will reflect your eligibility at the time you use the tool, including pre\-requisites, academic period and other factors\. 

### Tips for reviewing the Troubleshooting Registration page

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Section
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    How to review

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Academic Period**
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Check the “Academic Period” to make sure it shows: The correct session and term you are registering for\.  The correct campus\. For example, if you are registering for a course beginning in September 2026 on the Vancouver campus, the Academic Period should display “2026\-27 Winter Term 2 \(UBC\-V\)”\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Academic Record & Active Record**
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    The “Academic Record” should match your primary program of study, and must be listed as “Active” \(yes\)\. If your Academic Record is not listed as “Active”, you will not be able to register for the course\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Course & Course Section**
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Both the course and course section must be offered at the Vancouver campus in order for you to register\. If the course code is followed by “\_V”, it means that the course is offered on the Vancouver campus, if it ends with an “O” it is offered on the Vancouver campus For example, PSYC**\_V** 203, or PSYC**\_V** 203\-100 are courses offered at UBCV

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Enrol****ment Window**
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Make sure the “Enrolment Window” says “Yes”\. This means you are trying to register within the allowable time period\. You will not be able to register if you see “No” next to “Enrolment Window”\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Maximum** **Credits, Enrolled Credits and Additional Credits** **From** **This Course Section**
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Compare these values to ensure you are not trying to register for more than your maximum allowable credits for the academic period\.  
      
    1\. Review your “Maximum Credits”\.   
    2\. Add your “Enrolled Credits” to the “Additional Credits From This Course Section”\.  
      
    These two values must equal or be less than the “Maximum Credits” value\.  
      
    Example results:  
    Maximum Credits \= 15  
    Enrolled Credits \= 12  
    Additional Credits From This Course Section \= 4  
      
    In this example, the student is trying to register in 16 credits, which exceeds the maximum credit value of 15\. This student would not be able to register for the course\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Holds**
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    The “Holds” section indicates whether you have a hold on your account blocking you from registering for courses\.  
      
    If you see the number 0 next to the “Holds” section, this means you do not have any holds on your account\. If you see a numerical value of 1 or higher, this means you have a hold on your academic record\. Learn how to [resolve a hold on your academic record](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/resolving-a-hold-on-your-record/)\.

### Tips for reviewing the Course and Course Section tables

The “Course” and “Course Section” tables each have three columns: “Restriction”, “Can Register”, and “Details”\. 

#### Restriction

This column shows the requirements that need to be satisfied for you to register in the course section\. Restrictions you might see include: 

| Restriction | What this means |
| --- | --- |
| **Eligible** | If you are eligible for a course based on eligibility rules such as pre\-requisites, corequisites, and other restrictions\. |
| **No D****uplicate R****egistration** | If you are currently registered for a course, you cannot register for the course again\. |
| **Has P****ublished, Visible S****ections** | A course must have published sections before you can register for it\. |
| **Can R****egister for C****o****requisite** | Note: this field will always display “Yes” in Workday\. To review corequisites for a course, search for it on the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools)\. |
| **Can R****epeat** | If you have enrolled in this course before, this field specifies if you can take it again\. |
| **Access to Enrolment** | Typically, Enrolment Access is set at Campus Level \(Vancouver or Okanagan\) and/or Academic Level \(Graduate or Undergraduate\)\. Students must meet these rules to register for a course\. |
| **Has Capacity** | If the course does not have seats available, then you will not be able to register into this course section\. |
| **No Time Conflict Exists** | If you have already registered into a course section that occurs at the same time as this course section, then you will not be able to register\. |

#### Can Register

This column indicates whether you can register based on the restriction requirements\. 

-   **No**: You are unable to register for the course because you do not meet the restrictions\.
-   **Yes**: You can register for the course\. 

#### Details

This column provides further details about why restriction requirements are not met, if applicable\. 

## How to resolve registration issues

You may be able to resolve some issues on your own\. For more complex cases, you may need to speak to an academic advisor\. Review the information below to find out how to resolve common registration issues\.

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    **Restriction in Course/Course Sections table**
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    **Potential issue**
  
  - **Header cell 3:**
  
    **How to resolve**

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1 (rowspan 2):**
  
    Eligible
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    You are an undergraduate student trying to register for a graduate level course\.
  
  - **Cell 3:**
  
    You will not be able to self\-register in graduate courses\. To take graduate courses, [contact an academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    You have not taken the required prerequisites or corequisites for the course\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Take all the required prerequisites or corequisites before enrolling in the course\. To check which courses are required, review the course section in the [course schedule](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/)\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    No Time Conflict Exists
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    The course section overlaps with and belongs to the same course as another course section you’re already enrolled in\.
  
  - **Cell 3:**
  
    Decide which course section you want to enrol in and choose one\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Has Capacity
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    The course section has no capacity \(e\.g\. the course section is full or is closed\)\.
  
  - **Cell 3:**
  
    Select another course section or join the course waitlist if available\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    No Duplicate Registrations
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    You are already enrolled in the course section and are registering in the same section again\.
  
  - **Cell 3:**
  
    If you wish to remain in the current course section, no further action is required\. If you want to change to another section, [swap your course](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/swapping-dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course/)\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Can Repeat
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    You’ve reached maximum retake limit for the course but want to retake the course again\.
  
  - **Cell 3:**
  
    You will not be able to self\-register in the course unless you [contact an advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

**Please note:** 

In addition to the issues identified on the “Troubleshoot Registration” page, there may be other reasons that you are unable to register\. For example: 

-   **You have not successfully registered in prerequisite courses required for Term 2:** If you are taking a prerequisite course required for a Term 2 course during Term 1, you must successfully register for it before you can register for the Term 2 course\. Any alerts for Term 2 registration will be updated once you have registered for the prerequisite course in Term 1\. 
-   **Your Registration Appointment has not opened or the add/drop deadline has passed:** Learn how to [view your registration appointment](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-your-registration-appointment/)\. 
-   **You are an Vancouver campus student and try to register for a course on the UBC Okanagan campus:** Check the [course code](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/troubleshooting-your-course-registration/#course-code) to verify that the course is for the correct campus\. To take courses on the UBC Vancouver campus, please refer to the [Cross Campus Registration eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/cross-campus-registration/) and [contact an academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\. 

## Additional resources

title: Paying your tuition and student fees with Credit card and Signature Debit card payment
content_markdown:
## About TouchNet

UBC uses TouchNet as a payment tool for tuition and student fees\.

TouchNet is replacing other forms of ePayment, such as International Funds Transfer via Convera and Interac Online\.  

Receipts for payments made in TouchNet are only available in TouchNet, not in Workday\.

Please note that your TouchNet profile reflects your legal name\.

TouchNet accepts Visa, Mastercard, as well as major banks’ Visa Debit and Mastercard Debit cards\.

## How to pay with a credit card

### First, go to your Finances App  

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\.
2.  On the right side of the page, in the “Your Top Apps” menu, click the “Finances” app\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Go-to-your-finances-app.jpg)

### Review your current outstanding balance

In the Finances app, you will be taken to the “Finances” page by default\. 

On the left side of the page, under “Account Activity”, your “Due Now” balance will be listed\. This balance includes charges that are past due or due within the next 30 days\.

If there are any changes in your registration, program of study, or citizenship on your account, your account balance will be updated the following day\. Your Account Activity does not refresh in real time\. Tuition and student fees are assessed nightly\.

You can make payments toward your “Due Now” balance, but not charges due in the future\.

You may not see ‘Charges’ until you register in courses\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/WD-Outstanding-Balance-Before-Payment-1-940x272.jpg)

### Next, go to TouchNet Payment Centre

In the “Tuition and Fees” menu to the right, click the “Make a Payment: TouchNet Payment Centre” link\. You will be redirected to the TouchNet homepage, which is a separate app from Workday\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Go-to-TouchNet.jpg)

### Make a payment 

1.  Once on the TouchNet homepage, you will see your current outstanding balance listed as “Due Now” in the Student Account box\. Click the dark blue “Make Payment” button\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_make-payment--940x351.jpg)

2.  On the “Account Payment” page, enter the amount you want to pay in the field under “Amount Due”\. You have the option to make a full or partial payment\.
3.  Click the blue “Continue” button to the lower right\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_enter-amount-to-be-paid-940x454.jpg)

4.  If you’ve previously designated your pre\-authorized debit bank account as your default payment method, you will be prompted to pay with this method automatically\. To change to credit or debit card, you can click the blue “Cancel” button on the CAD Pre\-Auth Debit Payment Agreement, and select “Credit Card via PayPath” from the “Method” dropdown list\.
5.  Click the dark blue “Continue” button to the lower right\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_select-payment-method-940x378.jpg)

6.  You will be brought to a confirmation screen, where you can review your payment information, payment amount, and the terms and conditions\. After confirming your information, click the dark blue “Continue to PayPath” button to the lower right\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_review-payment-info-940x525.jpg)

6.  You’ll now complete the payment in the “PayPath” Payment Service\. Follow the instructions in the new window to complete the payment transaction\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_paypath-home-page-940x533.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_paypath-process-940x558.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_enter-card-info-and-address-940x606.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_review-transaction-940x692.jpg)

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_receipt-940x633.jpg)

### Confirm your payment

After you’ve paid, you will be returned to the TouchNet confirmation page, which summarizes payment receipt details\. While a receipt will be sent to your email, you have the option to print this page for your records\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/TouchNet_pay-using-credit_account-payment-confirmation-940x401.jpg)

### Check your Account Activity

Lastly, return to [Workday](http://www.myworkday.ubc.ca/) and refresh your browser\. Your “Due Now” balance will be updated and you will see a new transaction in your Account Activity reflecting your payment\.

You can click on the “View Statement” button for more information\.

[Image](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/05/Finance_Outstanding-balance-2-940x273.jpg)

title: Setting up your direct deposit
content_markdown:
Setting up your direct deposit allows you to receive payments directly into your bank account\. You may need to set up direct deposit in Workday to receive a refund, bursary or scholarship, funding from a US Loan, an expense reimbursement ,or a paycheque from UBC as a student staff\. 

To set up direct deposit information, you will need a chequing or savings account at a Canadian financial institution or bank\. You can find your banking information, like your Institution Number, Transit Number, and Account Number,in your account information in online banking\. Contact your financial institution for support if you are unable to locate this information\. 

## On this page:

-   [How to add your direct deposit information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/#add)
-   [How to edit your direct deposit information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/#edit)

## How to add your direct deposit information  

### Go to your Finances App in Workday

1.  Log into your Workday account at [myworkday\.ubc\.ca](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. 
2.  Select “Student” in the navigation bar on the left\. 
3.  Select “Finances”\.  

### Add your direct deposit information

1.  Select the “Direct Deposit \(Payment Elections\)” link in the “Banking Details” menu on the right\. 
2.  Click the “Add” button\. 
3.  A new pop\-up window will appear\.  In the “Preferred Payment Method” section, make sure the following types of payments are set to “Direct Deposit”:  
    -   **Student** **Refund****:** includes tuition credit refunds, award funding, and US loans\.  
    -   **Expenses****:** refers to expense reimbursements from UBC\.  
    -   **Regular****:** refers to payroll if you are a student staff\.  
4.  Complete the required fields indicated with a red asterisk mark \(\*\):   
    -   Institution Number   
    -   Account Number   
    -   Transit Number 

**Note:** If you have more than one bank account, you can choose to receive different payments in each\. For example, you can receive your scholarship money in a bank account that’s different from where you receive your student employee paycheque\. 

[Direct deposit page details](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/Direct-deposit_1.2_Final-1.jpg)

5\. Click “OK” to save your information\.

### Review your direct deposit information 

After saving your direct deposit information, you will be returned to the “Payment Elections” page\.

Your details will be listed in a table under “Payment Elections”\. Review your details to make sure you receive your direct deposits\.

[direct deposit info](https://student-workday-2024.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2026/08/Direct-deposit_2_Final-1-940x335.jpg)

## How to edit your direct deposit information

### First, go to the Direct Deposit \(Payment Elections\) page

1.  Follow the [steps above](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/#finances) to go to your Finances App\.
2.  Select the “Direct Deposit \(Payment Elections\)” link in the “Banking Details” menu on the right\.
3.  Under the “Accounts” table, use the buttons in the “Action” column to update your bank account information:  
    -   **Remove:** Remove a bank account from Workday\. If you are removing a bank account from your direct deposit information, make sure you remove this account from **all** payment elections before deleting it\.  
        -   Under the “Payment Elections” table, use the Edit button in the “Action” column to update a specific payment type, including the bank account a payment is deposited in\.   
    -   **View**: View your bank account details\.  
    -   **Add**: Add another bank account\.
